title: Part 5: Can Liberal Democracy Survive in Europe?

sentences.en: Hi, I'm Andrew Ross-Sorkin.
sentences.zh: 嗨，我是安德鲁·罗斯-索尔金。

sentences.en: I cover business and policy for Dealbook, a daily newsletter at the
sentences.zh: 我负责《纽约时报》每日时事通讯 Dealbook 的商业与政策报道。

sentences.en: New York Times.
sentences.zh: 《纽约时报》。

sentences.zh: 11 月 18 日，我将在纽约市 Dealbook 峰会的现场采访商业、政治和文化领域最具影响力的领袖，其中包括 J.D.

sentences.en: Vance, Elon Musk, Christine
sentences.zh: 万斯、埃隆·马斯克、克里斯蒂娜

sentences.en: Lagarde, Zylran Mondani, and many others, live on stage at the Dealbook Summit in New York City.
sentences.zh: 拉加德、齐尔兰·蒙达尼以及许多其他人。

sentences.zh: 你可以实时观看其中一些毫无防备、未经过滤的对话。

sentences.zh: 如果你还不是订阅者，可以下载《纽约时报》应用来观看，并免费获得我们所有新闻报道一个月的访问权限。

sentences.en: I hope you'll tune in.
sentences.zh: 希望大家锁定收看。

sentences.zh: 你一定不想错过。

sentences.en: So at this point, we're on the train platform in Warsaw.
sentences.zh: 所以在这一刻，我们正站在华沙的火车站台上。

sentences.en: We've been traveling together for a few weeks now.
sentences.zh: 我们已经一起旅行好几周了。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: And we've been going from country to country to sort of check what people are thinking ahead of these European elections, which are now upon us.
sentences.zh: 我们一直在各个国家之间穿梭，以便了解在这场欧洲议会选举即将来临之际，大家都在想些什么。

sentences.en: So we pack up and head to the train station in Poland
sentences.zh: 于是我们收拾行囊，前往波兰的火车站

sentences.en: and get on the train back to Berlin.
sentences.zh: 坐上了返回柏林的火车。

sentences.en: You know, we started this trip thinking that these liberal values that are so fundamental to the
sentences.zh: 你知道的，我们开始这次旅行时认为，那些作为欧盟创立基础、源自二战后极其核心的自由主义价值观，

sentences.en: founding of the European Union coming out of World War II, that they're now being rejected by all these
sentences.zh: 现在正被欧洲各地的所有这些运动所拒绝，被认为不再与人们的生活相关，甚至被视为对他们国家认同的威胁和强加的束缚。

sentences.en: movements across Europe as no longer relevant to people's lives or even as threats to their national identities, as impositions.
sentences.zh: 通过与波兰法律与公正党政治家达努塔的交谈，我觉得我更好地理解了这背后的含义，以及民粹主义者究竟想要一个什么样的欧洲。

sentences.en: Speaking with Danuta, the Polish law and justice politician, I think I understood a little bit better what this was about and what kind of Europe the populists wanted.
sentences.zh: 他们不是想抛弃民主。

sentences.en: They don't want to throw away democracy.
sentences.zh: 他们想抛弃的是自由主义。

sentences.en: They want to throw away liberalism.
sentences.zh: 他们想要一个能够回应他们、对他们负责、代表多数人意志的民主。

sentences.en: They want a democracy that responds to them, that answers to them, that represents the will of the majority.
sentences.zh: 这就是他们带入欧盟议会的那种较量。

sentences.en: And this is the battle they're kind of bringing to the EU parliament.
sentences.zh: 因此，这场选举——世界第二大民主进程——关乎有多少抱持这种不同欧洲愿景的人能够进入议会。

sentences.en: So these elections, the second biggest democratic process in the world, this is about how many of these people with a different vision of Europe get into the parliament.
sentences.zh: 这里是德国吗？

sentences.en: This is Germany?
sentences.zh: 这里是德国。

sentences.en: This is Germany.
sentences.zh: 我们正在穿越边境返回德国，这个位于自由欧洲核心的国家，

sentences.en: And so we're crossing the border back into Germany, this country at the heart of a liberal Europe,
sentences.zh: 故事正是在这里开始的，但民族主义也在这里获得了势头，如今这里还出现了一个极右翼政党——德国选择党（AfD）。

sentences.en: where the story began, but where nationalism has also gained traction, and where now there is this far-right party, the AFD.
sentences.zh: 我们想看看这种对欧洲的另一种看法、对自由主义的拒绝，在德国究竟占据了多大程度的影响力。

sentences.en: We wanted to see to what extent this other view of Europe, that rejection of liberalism, had taken hold in Germany too.
sentences.zh: 来自《纽约时报》，我是卡特琳·文德尔。

sentences.en: From the New York Times, I'm Katrin Wendel.
sentences.zh: 这里是《每日新闻》。

sentences.en: This is The Daily.
sentences.zh: 今天是，重返德国。

sentences.en: Today, back to Germany.
sentences.zh: 今天是 6 月 14 日，星期五。

sentences.en: It's Friday, June 14th.
sentences.zh: 所以在过去的三天里，整个欧盟的选民一直在前往投票站。

sentences.en: So for the last three days, voters across the European Union have been going to the polls.
sentences.zh: 而在最后一天，我们驱车大约 45 分钟来到柏林郊外，基本上是为了和

sentences.en: And on this last day, we drive something like 45 minutes to the outskirts of Berlin to basically spend the election night with the
sentences.zh: 德国极右翼政党——选择党一起度过选举之夜。

sentences.en: AFD, Germany's far-right party.
sentences.zh: 当我们下车时，立刻被一阵声浪所包围。

sentences.en: So we get out of the car, and we're just hit by this wall of sound.
sentences.zh: 那里大概有两打抗议者。

sentences.en: There's maybe two dozen protesters there.
sentences.zh: 他们拿着横幅，拿着扩音器，在呼喊，在叫嚷。

sentences.en: They have banners, they have megaphones, they're chanting, they're shouting.
sentences.zh: 警察试图控制他们。

sentences.en: There's police trying to sort of control them.
sentences.zh: 人群虽然不大，但非常喧闹。

sentences.en: It's not a big crowd, but it's a very noisy crowd.
sentences.zh: 他们基本上把选择党等同于纳粹。

sentences.en: They're basically equating the AFD to Nazis.
sentences.zh: 于是我们试图找到这个政党聚会的入口，并绕着建筑寻找。

sentences.en: So we're trying to find the entrance to this party, and we're making our way around the building.
sentences.zh: 后面有一种安检控制。

sentences.en: And there's this sort of security control at the back.
sentences.zh: 我们出示身份证，走过一个停车场。

sentences.en: We show our IDs, walk past a parking lot.
sentences.zh: 这到底是什么地方？

sentences.en: And what is this place?
sentences.zh: 这是一个舞蹈学校。

sentences.en: So this is, it's actually a dance school.
sentences.zh: 他们租了一所舞蹈学校，因为他们原本打算在一家餐馆举办选举聚会。

sentences.en: They've rented out a dance school because they were going to have their election party at a restaurant.
sentences.zh: 但餐馆老板收到了太多来自反选择党人士的威胁，以至于他们不得不更换地点。

sentences.en: And the restaurant owner received so many threats from like anti-AFD people that they had to move the location.
sentences.zh: 这一切都神神秘秘的。

sentences.en: It was all like hush-hush.
sentences.zh: 我们直到昨天才知道。

sentences.en: And we only found out yesterday.
sentences.zh: 但在任何其他日子，你都可以在这里学习跳探戈。

sentences.en: But on any other day, you can learn how to dance tango here.
sentences.zh: 最终我们来到了这个舞蹈学校，也就是今晚选择党聚会的场地。

sentences.en: And finally get to this dance school, which is tonight's venue for the AFD's party.
sentences.zh: 所以这不像那种美国风格的、伴随着气球和音乐的狂热选举派对。

sentences.en: So this isn't like a sort of US-style raging election party with balloons and music.
sentences.zh: 这相当具有德国特色。

sentences.en: This is fairly kind of German.
sentences.zh: 全都是男士。

sentences.en: It's only men.
sentences.zh: 看那儿。

sentences.en: Look at that.
sentences.zh: 或者说主要是男士。

sentences.en: Or mainly.
sentences.zh: 有很多穿着西装的男人，喝着啤酒，吃着蝴蝶酥，人们在等待晚上 11 点今晚的第一个真实结果。

sentences.en: There's a lot of men in suits, drinking beer, eating pretzels, as people kind of wait for the first real results of the evening at 11 p.m.
sentences.zh: 用英语吗？

sentences.en: In English?
sentences.zh: 你英语说得真棒。

sentences.en: You speak brilliant.
sentences.zh: 啊哈！

sentences.en: Aha!
sentences.zh: 好的，好的。

sentences.en: Okay, okay.
sentences.zh: 接着是约尔格·莫伊滕。

sentences.en: And then there's Jörg Meuthen.
sentences.zh: 我是约尔格·莫伊滕。

sentences.en: I'm Jörg Meuthen.
sentences.zh: 我是德国选择党的主席。

sentences.en: I'm the chair of the AFD of Germany.
sentences.zh: 约尔格是这次参选的选择党主要候选人。

sentences.en: So Jörg is the main candidate of the AFD running in these elections.
sentences.zh: 他已经在欧洲议会任职，但这次他正竞选连任。

sentences.en: He's already in the EU parliament, but he's running for re-election.
sentences.zh: 我在欧洲议会。

sentences.en: I'm in European parliament.
sentences.zh: 他可以说是当晚的明星。

sentences.en: He was kind of the star of the evening.
sentences.zh: 我想问他，他如何看待

sentences.en: And I want to ask him, what does he make of the state of
sentences.zh: 德国民主的现状？

sentences.en: German democracy?
sentences.zh: 他如何看待我们在波兰听到的那种观点，即德国民主程度有所下降？

sentences.en: And what does he make of this idea that we heard in Poland, that Germany is less democratic?
sentences.zh: 因为德国坚守这些自由主义价值观。

sentences.en: Because it adheres to these liberal values.
sentences.zh: 你认为今天的德国民主是健康的吗？

sentences.en: Do you think German democracy today is healthy?
sentences.zh: 于是我问了他们。

sentences.en: So I asked them.
sentences.zh: 不，它不健康。

sentences.en: No, it's not.
sentences.zh: 一点也不健康。

sentences.en: It's not at all.
sentences.zh: 民主在德国起作用吗？

sentences.en: Is democracy working in Germany?
sentences.zh: 例如，有这么多人与我们作对。

sentences.en: For example, there are so many people fighting against us.
sentences.zh: 他们说，我们是纳粹，我们是种族主义者，我们是反犹太主义者，诸如此类。

sentences.en: They say, we are Nazis, we are racist, we are anti-Semitic, and all these things.
sentences.zh: 这完全、真的、完全是错误的。

sentences.en: It's completely, really, completely wrong.
sentences.zh: 约尔格说，不，民主没有在起作用。

sentences.en: And Jörg said, no, democracy is not working.
sentences.zh: 例如，他们不接受我们今天在这里举行选举派对。

sentences.en: They do not accept, for example, that we have our election party here today.
sentences.zh: 他们试图用暴力把我们赶出去。

sentences.en: They try to get us out from here by using violence.
sentences.zh: 他说，看，看看我们在哪里。

sentences.en: He said, look, look where we're at.
sentences.zh: 我们在柏林郊外的这个舞厅里，因为我们在另一个地方受到了威胁。

sentences.en: We're in this dance hall on the outskirts of Berlin, because we were threatened in this other place.
sentences.zh: 他们通过烧毁我们的汽车、对个人进行肉体暴力来与我们对抗。

sentences.en: And they fight against us by burning down our cars, by fighting with a physical kind of violence against persons.
sentences.zh: 这不是一种健康的民主。

sentences.en: And that's not a healthy kind of democracy.
sentences.zh: 我需要保镖，大量的保镖。

sentences.en: I need bodyguards, a large number of bodyguards.
sentences.zh: 你身后那个是你的保镖吗？

sentences.en: Is that your bodyguard behind you?
sentences.zh: 举个例子。

sentences.en: For example.
sentences.zh: 那边还有一个，对吧？

sentences.en: Another one there, no?
sentences.zh: 他们中的一些人在这里。

sentences.en: Some of them are here.
sentences.zh: 这是必需的，因为如果我出门，对我很危险。

sentences.en: And it's necessary, because if I go out, it's dangerous for me.
sentences.zh: 为什么？

sentences.en: Why?
sentences.zh: 为什么？

sentences.en: Why?
sentences.zh: 我只是持有一种观点。

sentences.en: I just have an opinion.
sentences.zh: 我能接受别人不接受我的观点。

sentences.en: And I can accept that others do not accept my opinion.
sentences.zh: 他说，看，我们甚至不能说出我们的想法。

sentences.en: And he said, look, we can't even say what we think.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，我总是会为左翼争取表达他们想做的事情的权利而战，因为那是民主，那是自由。

sentences.en: You know, I would always fight for the left side to have the right to say what they want to do, because that's democracy and that's freedom.
sentences.zh: 但左翼却不接受我们。

sentences.en: But from the left side, they do not accept us.
sentences.zh: 他说，自由主义者引以为豪的宽容，在遇到像他这样的观点时就戛然而止了，那些他们不喜欢观点。

sentences.en: He says that the tolerance that liberals pride themselves on ends with opinions like his, opinions that they don't like.
sentences.zh: 在一个言论自由日益困难的社会里，要维持民主是很艰难的。

sentences.en: It's difficult to have a democracy where free speech is getting more difficult every day.
sentences.zh: 这种挫败感在这里经常被表达出来。

sentences.en: This frustration is voiced a lot here.
sentences.zh: 在德国，如果你说我是选择党党员，你就租不到公寓吗？

sentences.en: In Germany, you say, I'm from the AfD, and you don't get a Wohnung?
sentences.zh: 你租不到公寓？

sentences.en: You don't get an apartment?
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 如果你说了这个，你就租不到公寓。

sentences.en: You can't rent an apartment if you say this.
sentences.zh: 在今天的汉堡，如果你想成为一名教师，你必须签署一份声明，保证我不是选择党党员。

sentences.en: In Hamburg today, if you want to be a teacher, you must make a signature that I don't in the AfD.
sentences.zh: 我是选择党的成员。

sentences.en: I'm a member of the AfD.
sentences.zh: 这并不自由。

sentences.en: That's not free.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，无论你是否同意政府的政策，

sentences.en: You know, whether or not you agree with the policy of the government or not,
sentences.zh: 或者你完全反对它，在一个民主国家，公开讨论这些问题不应该是个问题。

sentences.en: or you oppose it completely, in a democracy, it should not be a problem to address those problems in public.
sentences.zh: 你不需要害怕失去工作，或者遭到攻击之类的事情。

sentences.en: And you don't have to be afraid of, you know, losing your job, you know, getting attacked or something.
sentences.zh: 特别是在柏林，许多人，像我这样年纪较大的来自东德的人，今天感觉就像回到了家一样。

sentences.en: Especially in Berlin, a lot of people, older people like me, that they came from East Germany, feels today like coming home.
sentences.zh: 这是同样的体制，同样的压力。

sentences.en: It's the same system, it's the same pressure.
sentences.zh: 在工作中，你要环顾四周，注意自己说的话，而这是全新的。

sentences.en: At work, you look over your shoulder, what you're saying, and this is new.
sentences.zh: 所以你是说这让你想起了共产主义？

sentences.en: So you're saying this reminds you of communism?
sentences.zh: 绝对是的。

sentences.en: Absolutely.
sentences.zh: 这是同样的压力，只是更聪明了，而且还是彩色的。

sentences.en: It's the same pressure, it's smarter, and it's in color.
sentences.zh: 但这和共产主义时期是同一堆屎。

sentences.en: But it's the same shit like in the communism.
sentences.zh: 这个想法并非完全异想天开，因为德国由于其历史原因，确实有一些特殊情况。

sentences.en: And this isn't an entirely wild idea in the sense that Germany, because of its history, again, has some special circumstances.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，在德国，仇恨言论法极其严格，以至于对一个美国人来说，这几乎看起来像是审查制度。

sentences.en: I mean, in Germany, hate speech laws are extremely strict, to the point where, to an American, this may almost seem like censorship.
sentences.zh: 例如，你不能在公共场合展示纳粹万字旗。

sentences.en: You can't, for example, show a swastika in public.
sentences.zh: 那是犯罪。

sentences.en: That's a crime.
sentences.zh: 因此，由于仇恨言论法，德国的言论自由比许多其他民主国家受到的限制更多。

sentences.en: So freedom of speech is more curtailed in Germany because of hate speech laws than it is in a lot of other democracies.
sentences.zh: 所以他们认为自己遭到了不公正的针对。

sentences.en: So they see themselves as unfairly targeted.
sentences.zh: 那么，到底是什么话是他们想说却觉得不能说的呢？

sentences.en: So what is it that they want to say that they feel like they can't?
sentences.zh: 那么，有什么话是你希望在工作说，但又觉得同事不让你说的呢？

sentences.en: And so what is it that you would like to say at work and you feel your colleagues don't let you say?
sentences.zh: 我想说出我的真实感受。

sentences.en: I want to talk what I feel.
sentences.zh: 我们多次问过这个问题，而人们总是绕弯子。

sentences.en: We asked this several times, and people sort of talk around it.
sentences.zh: 安全、教育、边境安全。

sentences.en: Safety, education, border security.
sentences.zh: 一个经常被提及的问题是他们对伊斯兰教的看法。

sentences.en: And one thing that came up a lot is their views on Islam.
sentences.zh: 如果你对从各个国家来到这里的移民持有某种看法，

sentences.en: If you have a certain opinion about the immigrants that come here from all different countries,
sentences.zh: 如果你说，嗯，我认为他们没有留在这里的合法身份，你就会被归类为右翼人士。

sentences.en: if you say, well, I believe they do not have the legal status to stay here, you're classified as a right-wing person.
sentences.zh: 有一种感觉，如果你表达了对移民或伊斯兰教的厌恶，你就会冒着被称为纳粹的风险。

sentences.en: There's a sort of sense that if you express, for example, your dislike of immigration or of Islam, that you run the risk of being called a Nazi.
sentences.zh: 而他们说，我们为身为德国人感到自豪是可以的。

sentences.en: And they're saying, it's okay for us to be proud to be German.
sentences.zh: 我们想要庆祝自己的文化是可以的。

sentences.en: It's okay for us to want to celebrate our culture.
sentences.zh: 反对移民是可以的。

sentences.en: It's okay to be opposed to immigration.
sentences.zh: 这并不意味着我们是纳粹。

sentences.en: That doesn't make us Nazis.
sentences.zh: 他们某种程度上想要的就是达努塔——那位来自波兰民族主义政党的波兰法律与公正党政治家——对我们所讲的那种东西。

sentences.en: They kind of want what Danuta, that Polish law and justice politician from the Nationalist Party in Poland, told us about.
sentences.zh: 他们希望多数人基本上拥有最后决定权。

sentences.en: They want the majority to basically get the last word.
sentences.zh: 但当我们拥有一个选择党政府时，社会将会更加民主，因为我们希望由人民来决定某些事情。

sentences.en: But we will be more democratic when we have an AFD government because we want the people to decide certain things.
sentences.zh: 他们认为，欧洲各地民粹主义的崛起远非对民主的威胁，实际上是一个健康、充满活力的民主的标志。

sentences.en: They argue that the rise of populism across Europe, far from being a threat to democracy, it's actually a sign of a healthy, vibrant one.
sentences.zh: 但当你把所有权力都交给多数人时，你也剥夺了对少数群体的保护。

sentences.en: But when you give all the power to the majority, you also take protections away from minorities.
sentences.zh: 所以我很好奇，在什么情况下这会成为一个问题？

sentences.en: And so I'm wondering, at what point is this a problem?
sentences.zh: 如果人们随后投票赞成死刑呢？

sentences.en: What if the people then vote in favor of the death penalty?
sentences.zh: 如果人们随后投票赞成死刑呢？

sentences.en: One issue that to me as a German and as a European felt like a good pressure test is the death penalty.
sentences.zh: 作为一个德国人和欧洲人，我觉得有一个问题就像是一次很好的压力测试，那就是死刑。

sentences.en: Across the political spectrum, including the AFD, everybody here in Germany is against the death penalty,
sentences.zh: 在整个政治光谱中，包括选择党（AFD）在内，德国这里的每个人都反对死刑，

sentences.en: which has been illegal in democratic Germany since World War II and the Nazi era.
sentences.zh: 自二战和纳粹时期以来，死刑在民主德国一直是违法的。

sentences.en: Then you think, well, if the majority of the people say we want the death penalty back, do you think that actually maybe the government needs to bring the death penalty back?
sentences.zh: 然后你会想，好吧，如果多数人说我们想要恢复死刑，你觉得政府是不是真的应该把死刑恢复呢？

sentences.en: When I asked, they would just say this would never happen.
sentences.zh: 当我问他们时，他们只会说这绝不会发生。

sentences.en: It would never happen.
sentences.zh: 这绝不可能发生。

sentences.en: But I said, what if they did?
sentences.zh: 但我说，如果发生了呢？

sentences.en: Should it be?
sentences.zh: 应该这样吗？

sentences.en: I mean, is that what you're saying?
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，这就是你的意思吗？

sentences.en: A referendum should, if the people say something, it should happen?
sentences.zh: 如果人民说了什么，公投就应该让它发生吗？

sentences.en: I hope the education and Erfahrung,
sentences.zh: 我希望教育和经验（Erfahrung），

sentences.en: Memory or the experience, are on a level today that this, like your Beispiel, this example are not possible.
sentences.zh: 记忆或经历，在今天已经达到了这样的水平：像你说的这个例子（Beispiel）这种事是不可能的。

sentences.en: I hope we are working to avoid.
sentences.zh: 我希望我们正在努力避免这种情况。

sentences.en: Basically, they were saying, we trust that our people wouldn't do that.
sentences.zh: 基本上，他们的意思是，我们相信我们的人民不会做出那种事。

sentences.en: Our people know better.
sentences.zh: 我们的人民心里有数。

sentences.en: Our people can handle direct democracy.
sentences.zh: 我们的人民能够驾驭直接民主。

sentences.en: They wouldn't vote for that kind of thing.
sentences.zh: 他们不会投票支持那种东西。

sentences.en: And I kept asking, what if they did?
sentences.zh: 而我一直追问，如果他们真的投了呢？

sentences.en: And after many, many rounds of this, one agreed.
sentences.zh: 在经历了无数轮这样的对话后，终于有人同意了。

sentences.en: Yes, of course.
sentences.zh: 是的，当然。

sentences.en: That's democracy.
sentences.zh: 这就是民主。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Then we'd have to do it.
sentences.zh: 那我们就必须照做。

sentences.en: That's a kind of basic democracy.
sentences.zh: 这是一种基础民主。

sentences.en: And if the German people vote in a referendum, we don't want any more MusliMs.
sentences.zh: 如果德国人民在公投中投票说，我们不再想要任何穆斯林了，

sentences.en: Because I meet people, especially in East Germany and Saxony, who say, we just don't want any more MusliMs.
sentences.zh: 因为我遇到了一些人，特别是在东德和萨克森州，他们说，我们就是不想要更多穆斯林了。

sentences.en: If the people say that they don't want any more Muslims, is that what democracy dictates, that actually stop?
sentences.zh: 如果人民说他们不想要更多穆斯林了，难道民主就决定了这一切必须停止吗？

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: That's it.
sentences.zh: 就是这样。

sentences.en: This sort of raises inevitably the question in Germany, this country with our history, right?
sentences.zh: 这在德国不可避免地引发了一个问题，这个拥有我们这样历史的国家，对吧？

sentences.en: We once targeted a group, a religious group, in our paSt.
sentences.zh: 我们在过去曾经针对过一个群体，一个宗教群体。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 对。

sentences.en: And the narrative was similar.
sentences.zh: 而且当时的说法也很相似。

sentences.en: They're not compatible.
sentences.zh: 他们是无法融入的。

sentences.en: They want to destroy us from the inside and all of this.
sentences.zh: 他们想从内部摧毁我们，诸如此类。

sentences.en: So what's different?
sentences.zh: 那现在有什么不同？

sentences.en: We Germans have learned a lot from the thing with World War II, the Shoah Holocaust, you know.
sentences.zh: 我们德国人从二战、犹太人大屠杀（Shoah）这件事情中学到了很多，你知道的。

sentences.en: And the members from this party have learned that no man in history has damaged this country so much like Adolf Hitler.
sentences.zh: 这个党的成员也认识到，历史上没有任何人像阿道夫·希特勒那样对这个国家造成了如此巨大的破坏。

sentences.en: They want conservative rights, views.
sentences.zh: 他们想要保守的权利和观点。

sentences.en: They want law and order, I think.
sentences.zh: 我想他们想要法律和秩序。

sentences.en: But nothing with Nazi.
sentences.zh: 但绝不跟纳粹沾边。

sentences.en: Nothing to do with it.
sentences.zh: 跟那没有任何关系。

sentences.en: Again and again, as we make our way through this election party and we talk to people,
sentences.zh: 在这次选举派对上，随着我们不断与人们交谈，一次又一次地，

sentences.en: I kept bringing up the fact that Hitler himself was elected.
sentences.zh: 我不断提及这样一个事实：希特勒本人就是通过选举上台的。

sentences.en: He's a product of a democratic process.
sentences.zh: 他是民主程序的产物。

sentences.en: And this one young guy said something.
sentences.zh: 然后有个年轻小伙子说了句话。

sentences.en: He said something that we've been hearing from young people across Europe on this trip,
sentences.zh: 他说了我们在这次行程中从欧洲各地年轻人那里听到过的话，

sentences.en: but it's especially meaningful to hear it in Germany.
sentences.zh: 但在德国听到这话，感觉格外有意义。

sentences.en: We do have a certain history, but we are not the same people as at that time.
sentences.zh: 我们确实有某种历史，但我们已经不是当时的那拨人了。

sentences.en: He said that we should be able to leave the past behind.
sentences.zh: 他说我们应该能够把过去抛在脑后。

sentences.en: We shouldn't be limited to a history that is more than 80 years old.
sentences.zh: 我们不应被一个已有80多年历史的历史包袱所束缚。

sentences.en: I mean, take me as an example.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，拿我举个例子。

sentences.en: I have not been alive at that time.
sentences.zh: 我当时都还没出生。

sentences.en: My parents have not been living in that country you are talking of.
sentences.zh: 我的父母也没有生活在你所说的那种国家里。

sentences.en: Why should I be forced to say or to think something people want me to think?
sentences.zh: 为什么非要强迫我说出或去想那些别人希望我想的事情？

sentences.en: I live in the Germany of now and here.
sentences.zh: 我生活在此时此地的德国。

sentences.en: Are they firm results or they're still exocult?
sentences.zh: 这些是最终结果还是依然成谜？

sentences.en: And then, after hanging out at this party for a few hours, it's 11 p.m.
sentences.zh: 在参加了这个党的派对几个小时后，时间已经是晚上11点。

sentences.en: And the election results are coming in from all across Europe
sentences.zh: 当我们回来时，

sentences.en: when we come back.
sentences.zh: 欧洲各地的选举结果正陆续传来。

sentences.en: The New York Times app?
sentences.zh: 《纽约时报》App？

sentences.en: Unlocked?
sentences.zh: 已解锁？

sentences.en: Everyone knows you need to subscribe to The Times to access all of the reporting.
sentences.zh: 大家都知道，你需要订阅《时报》才能阅读所有报道。

sentences.en: But what if you could explore The Times for a month, for free, without putting in a credit card?
sentences.zh: 但是，如果你能免费试用《时报》一个月，且无需输入信用卡信息呢？

sentences.en: Now you can.
sentences.zh: 现在你可以了。

sentences.en: When you download The New York Times app for the first time, your first month in the app is free.
sentences.zh: 当你首次下载《纽约时报》App时，你在App内的第一个月是免费的。

sentences.en: A month to go behind the paywall to see what Times subscribers get every single day.
sentences.zh: 有一个月的时间突破付费墙，看看《时报》订阅者每天都能获得什么内容。

sentences.en: If you don't already subscribe to The New York Times, download The Times app today and get free access for 30 days.
sentences.zh: 如果你还没有订阅《纽约时报》，今天就下载《时报》App，获取30天的免费访问权限。

sentences.en: We've just had these TVs in the background all night and we've seen Salvini, we've seen the yellow vest, we've seen just like our whole trip,
sentences.zh: 整个晚上，我们身后的这些电视一直开着，我们看到了萨尔维尼，看到了黄马甲，就像我们的整个旅程一样，

sentences.en: it's just been on TV in the background all night.
sentences.zh: 一整晚电视上都在播这些。

sentences.en: So everyone at this AFD election party is kind of watching this big projector on the wall
sentences.zh: 所以，AFD这场选举派对上的每个人都在盯着墙上巨大的投影仪，

sentences.en: that has life results streaming in.
sentences.zh: 上面正在滚动播放实时结果。

sentences.en: This is the results?
sentences.zh: 这是结果吗？

sentences.en: This is Italy.
sentences.zh: 这是意大利。

sentences.en: This is Italy.
sentences.zh: 这是意大利。

sentences.en: And so eyes are glued on the screen and we're seeing the first results come in and it's very clear.
sentences.zh: 因此，大家的目光都紧盯着屏幕，我们看着第一批结果出炉，情况非常明朗。

sentences.en: The Democrats lost 20 points?
sentences.zh: 民主党人丢了20个百分点？

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: That the nationalists have done well in a number of countries.
sentences.zh: 民族主义者在许多国家都表现不错。

sentences.en: Sounds like Marine Le Pen has just been declared.
sentences.zh: 听起来玛丽娜·勒庞刚刚宣布胜选。

sentences.en: Oh wow, look.
sentences.zh: 哦，哇，你看。

sentences.en: In France, Marine Le Pen's party overtook Emmanuel Macron's in Italy.
sentences.zh: 在法国，玛丽娜·勒庞的党派在意大利超过了埃马纽埃尔·马克龙的党派。

sentences.en: Here comes the lead.
sentences.zh: 领先优势来了。

sentences.en: Oh my.
sentences.zh: 噢天哪。

sentences.en: The big winner was Salvini's party.
sentences.zh: 最大的赢家是萨尔维尼的党派。

sentences.en: There you go, the AFD, the German populace, are cheering the Italian populace.
sentences.zh: 你看，AFD，德国的民粹主义者，正在为意大利的民粹主义者欢呼。

sentences.en: And in Poland, it was Law and Justice that did the beSt.
sentences.zh: 在波兰，法律与公正党（Law and Justice）表现最好。

sentences.en: This is now Germany.
sentences.zh: 现在轮到德国了。

sentences.en: But when we get to Germany, it's not looking so good for the AFD.
sentences.zh: 但当我们把目光转向德国，对AFD来说情况似乎不太妙。
AFD，10月8日。

sentences.en: 11%, so it hasn't touched much.
sentences.zh: 11%，所以没怎么动。

sentences.en: They get 11%, which is a modest increase from where they were at at the last European election.
sentences.zh: 他们获得了11%的选票，与上届欧洲议会选举相比，这是一个微弱的增长。

sentences.en: But it's less than even what they got in the last national election.
sentences.zh: 但甚至比他们在上届联邦大选中获得的选票还要少。

sentences.en: And their rival party, the Greens, this center-left, pro-liberal, pro-refugee party that's essentially an anti-AFD party, the Greens get almost twice the vote that the AFD gets.
sentences.zh: 而他们的对手绿党——这个中左翼、亲自由派、亲难民、本质上是反AFD的政党——绿党获得的选票几乎是AFD的两倍。

sentences.en: And the mood in the room is subdued.
sentences.zh: 房间里的气氛十分低沉。

sentences.en: What do you make of tonight's result?
sentences.zh: 你如何看待今晚的结果？

sentences.en: Are you happy?
sentences.zh: 你高兴吗？

sentences.en: Well, yes, yes.
sentences.zh: 嗯，是的，是的。

sentences.en: All in all, I'm happy.
sentences.zh: 总的来说，我很高兴。

sentences.en: You always can have in mind more, more, more.
sentences.zh: 你心里总会想要更多、更多、更多。

sentences.en: But it's a fine result.
sentences.zh: 但这是一个不错的结果。

sentences.en: 11% is a good result and is a quite good reason to be happy and to have a good beer.
sentences.zh: 11%是个好结果，也是一个挺充分的理由去高兴，去喝上一杯好啤酒。

sentences.en: And overall, what's kind of the major headline of the night?
sentences.zh: 总的来说，今晚最大的头条新闻是什么？

sentences.en: So, it's a really mixed picture.
sentences.zh: 所以，这是一个非常复杂的局面。

sentences.en: One interpretation is to say that this sort of nationalist, populist wave wave that had been expected by some and predicted in the European Parliament
sentences.zh: 一种解读是，某些人所期望并在欧洲议会中预测的那种民族主义、民粹主义浪潮，

sentences.en: hasn't materialized.
sentences.zh: 并没有出现。

sentences.en: You know, we've seen an increase from 20% to about 24% of the seats now held by nationalists.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，我们看到民族主义者所占的议席比例从20%上升到了大约24%。

sentences.en: That's enough to make a lot of noise, maybe to disrupt proceedings to a certain degree, but you still have like three quarters of this body that is firmly on the pro-European,
sentences.zh: 这足以制造很多噪音，也许在一定程度上扰乱议程，但你仍然有大约四分之三的议员坚定地站在亲欧洲、

sentences.en: pro-liberal democracy side.
sentences.zh: 亲自由民主的一边。

sentences.en: The other interpretation is to say if you had told me
sentences.zh: 另一种解读是，如果你在10年前告诉我，

sentences.en: 10 years ago that there would be a far-right party in the German parliament and that this far-right party would get 11% in a European election and if you told me five years ago
sentences.zh: 德国议会里会有一个极右翼政党，而且这个极右翼政党在欧洲选举中能拿到11%；如果你在5年前告诉我，

sentences.en: that Salvini's League, which got 6% at the time, would now be on 34%,
sentences.zh: 当时仅获得6%选票的萨尔维尼联盟现在能达到34%，

sentences.en: I'd have been shocked.
sentences.zh: 我一定会大吃一惊。

sentences.en: These parties, these movements are now firmly entrenched everywhere in the EU, including in Germany.
sentences.zh: 这些政党、这些运动现在已经在欧盟各地（包括德国）牢固根深蒂固。

sentences.en: So what are you doing?
sentences.zh: 你们在做什么？

sentences.en: Just checking the results of our friend
sentences.zh: 只是在查看我们朋友的选举结果，

sentences.en: Susanna Ciccardi, the mayor.
sentences.zh: 市长苏珊娜·奇卡尔迪（Susanna Ciccardi）。

sentences.en: So now we just kind of want to check in with some of the people we'd met along the way to see, you know, what those results mean for them and for their countries.
sentences.zh: 所以现在我们想和一路上遇到的一些人聊聊，看看这些结果对他们和他们的国家意味着什么。

sentences.en: Ciao, Susanna!
sentences.zh: 嗨，苏珊娜！

sentences.en: It's Katrin from the New York Times.
sentences.zh: 我是《纽约时报》的卡特琳。

sentences.en: Ciao!
sentences.zh: 嗨！

sentences.en: So Susanna, whom we'd met in Italy, the candidate for Salvini's
sentences.zh: 苏珊娜是我们之前在意大利遇到的候选人，

sentences.en: Lega party.
sentences.zh: 代表萨尔维尼的联盟党（Lega）。

sentences.en: So what happened?
sentences.zh: 那么发生了什么？

sentences.en: Did you win?
sentences.zh: 你赢了吗？

sentences.en: No.
sentences.zh: 没有。

sentences.en: Wow, okay.
sentences.zh: 哇，好吧。

sentences.en: She won her seat.
sentences.zh: 她赢得了议席。

sentences.en: So you're going to the European Parliament?
sentences.zh: 所以你要去欧洲议会了？

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: So what's next?
sentences.zh: 接下来呢？

sentences.en: Salvini for prime minister?
sentences.zh: 萨尔维尼要当首相吗？

sentences.en: So this means that Matteo Salvini, who currently is interior minister, could conceivably force a new election, in which case, looking at these results, his party, the League party,
sentences.zh: 这意味着目前担任内政部长的马泰奥·萨尔维尼很可能会强行举行新的选举，在这种情况下，从这些结果来看，他的政党——联盟党，

sentences.en: would probably win and then Salvini
sentences.zh: 可能会获胜，然后萨尔维尼

sentences.en: Salvini, yes, would become the prime minister.
sentences.zh: 萨尔维尼，是的，就会成为首相。

sentences.en: I hope.
sentences.zh: 我希望如此。

sentences.en: You hope so.
sentences.zh: 你希望这样。

sentences.en: Well, do you think
sentences.zh: 那么，你认为

sentences.en: Salvini's vision for Europe is winning?
sentences.zh: 萨尔维尼对欧洲的愿景正在取胜吗？

sentences.en: Then finally, we call Magdalena,
sentences.zh: 最后，我们给玛格达莱娜打电话，

sentences.en: the candidate who we met in Poland and who's been running against the nationalist government there.
sentences.zh: 她在波兰被我们遇到，一直在与那里的民族主义政府竞选对抗。

sentences.en: Of course.
sentences.zh: 当然。

sentences.en: So did you win?
sentences.zh: 那你赢了吗？

sentences.en: Yes, yes, I win.
sentences.zh: 是的，是的，我赢了。

sentences.en: Congratulations.
sentences.zh: 恭喜。

sentences.en: And I have the best, the best result in our region.
sentences.zh: 而且我拿到了我们地区最好、最好的结果。

sentences.en: That is a huge vote of confidence.
sentences.zh: 这是一次巨大的信任投票。

sentences.en: Wow.
sentences.zh: 哇。

sentences.en: Actually, I'm very sad after this election, you know, because I...
sentences.zh: 其实，这次选举结束后我很难过，你知道的，因为我……

sentences.en: But she was very sad about the fact that the opposition overall had done poorly and that the government had done very, very well.
sentences.zh: 但她非常难过的是，总体而言反对派表现糟糕，而政府表现得非常非常出色。

sentences.en: Before we really believed that we win this election, then it would be this anniversary.
sentences.zh: 在我们真正相信我们能赢得这场选举之前，接着就会迎来这个周年纪念日。

sentences.en: And she said that she was worried that liberal democracy was losing.
sentences.zh: 她说她担心自由民主正在走向失败。

sentences.en: But liberal democracy is losing with populism.
sentences.zh: 但自由民主正伴随着民粹主义走向失败。

sentences.en: I see now people are losing their home.
sentences.zh: 我看到现在人们正失去他们的家园。

sentences.en: Well, good luck,
sentences.zh: 好吧，祝你好运，

sentences.en: Magdalena.
sentences.zh: 玛格达莱娜。

sentences.en: Good luck and thank you for giving us so much time.
sentences.zh: 祝你好运，也谢谢你给了我们这么多时间。

sentences.en: So by the time we get off the phone, the party is totally over.
sentences.zh: 因此，等我们挂断电话时，派对已经彻底结束了。

sentences.en: Should we take a cab with you and then we'll take a cab the rest of the way?
sentences.zh: 我们跟你一起坐出租车，然后剩下的路我们再自己打车？

sentences.en: You just keep going.
sentences.zh: 你只管往前走就行。

sentences.en: And the trip and the elections are over.
sentences.zh: 而且这趟行程和选举都结束了。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: So when we set out on this journey, we had all these questions about what would be the future of Europe?
sentences.zh: 所以当我们踏上这段旅程时，我们满脑子都是关于欧洲未来会怎样的疑问？

sentences.en: Would the European Union survive?
sentences.zh: 欧盟能生存下去吗？

sentences.en: And now that we've come back from our journey and seen these election results, do you feel like you have the answers to those questions now?
sentences.zh: 而现在，当我们结束了旅程、看到了这些选举结果，你觉得你现在找到这些问题的答案了吗？

sentences.en: I guess one of my biggest takeaways is that I don't think we have a Europe problem.
sentences.zh: 我想我最大的收获之一是，我不认为我们面临的是一个欧洲问题。

sentences.en: I think we have a democracy problem.
sentences.zh: 我认为我们面临的是一个民主问题。

sentences.en: For a lot of people we met, liberal democracy is just not delivering anymore.
sentences.zh: 对于我们遇到的许多人来说，自由民主已经不再兑现它的承诺了。

sentences.en: These values that the EU was founded on, they're just not making sense anymore in a lot of people's lives.
sentences.zh: 欧盟赖以成立的这些价值观，在许多人的生活中已经变得毫无意义。

sentences.en: You know, the electrician in France who has seen his salary stagnate and who's kind of humiliated to tell his own children in the middle of the month that there won't be
sentences.zh: 你知道的，法国的那名电工，他看着自己的薪水停滞不前，在月中时，他甚至有些难以启齿地告诉自己的孩子们，将没有

sentences.en: enough money.
sentences.zh: 足够的钱。

sentences.en: Or the Italian who doesn't feel at home anymore in their own small town after migrants moved in.
sentences.zh: 或者那个意大利人，在移民搬来之后，在自己的小镇里再也找不到家的感觉了。

sentences.en: Or the Polish person who feels that their Catholic values are being sort of fundamentally threatened.
sentences.zh: 或者那个波兰人，觉得他们的天主教价值观正受到某种根本性的威胁。

sentences.en: Each of these people is rejecting the tenets of liberal democracy, capitalism, globalization, the protection of minorities.
sentences.zh: 这些人中的每一个人都在排斥自由民主、资本主义、全球化以及对少数群体的保护这些原则。

sentences.en: because in a way each of these tenets feels like a rejection of them.
sentences.zh: 因为在某种程度上，这些原则中的每一项都让他们感觉自己被排斥了。

sentences.en: And I see that in my own country here in Germany.
sentences.zh: 我在我自己的国家德国也看到了这一点。

sentences.en: You know, the AFD is much more popular in the former communist East than it is in the WeSt.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，选择党（AfD）在曾经共产主义的东部比在西部要受欢迎得多。

sentences.en: And there's a reason for that.
sentences.zh: 这背后是有原因的。

sentences.en: East Germany had a very different experience of liberal democracy.
sentences.zh: 东德对自由民主有着截然不同的体验。

sentences.en: I grew up in Western Germany.
sentences.zh: 我在西德长大。

sentences.en: We got liberal democracy after World War II.
sentences.zh: 我们在二战后迎来了自由民主。

sentences.en: My story of liberal democracy is the post-war economic miracle.
sentences.zh: 我对自由民主的记忆是战后经济奇迹。

sentences.en: It's a good time.
sentences.zh: 那是一段美好的时光。

sentences.en: It's a happy time.
sentences.zh: 那是一段幸福的时光。

sentences.en: Things get better.
sentences.zh: 生活越来越好。

sentences.en: In the East, they got liberal democracy after communism fell and Germany was reunited.
sentences.zh: 而在东德，他们是在共产主义倒台、德国统一之后才获得自由民主的。

sentences.en: This is the 1990s.
sentences.zh: 那是20世纪90年代。

sentences.en: And it was followed by this very traumatic decade.
sentences.zh: 随之而来的是一个极其痛苦的十年。

sentences.en: You know, factories closed.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，工厂倒闭了。

sentences.en: There was mass unemployment.
sentences.zh: 出现了大规模失业。

sentences.en: Young people left in droves.
sentences.zh: 年轻人大批离开。

sentences.en: And Westerners came in to run everything.
sentences.zh: 而西方人涌入来接管一切。

sentences.en: Political parties, universities, businesses.
sentences.zh: 政党、大学、企业。

sentences.en: So East Germans who had just beaten communism in this incredible peaceful revolution,
sentences.zh: 所以，刚刚通过这场不可思议的和平革命击败了共产主义的东德人，

sentences.en: they ended up basically being told what to do by the WeSt.
sentences.zh: 到头来基本上沦落到听从西方的颐指气使。

sentences.en: And so when the AFD says liberalism has failed, you can sort of understand why East Germans agree with them.
sentences.zh: 因此，当选择党说自由主义已经失败时，你有点能理解为什么东德人会同意他们的看法了。

sentences.en: This is kind of what I've learned, that the rejection of liberalism
sentences.zh: 这就是我所学到的，对自由主义的排斥

sentences.en: often feels like a story that is born in disappointment and in humiliation and a feeling of being left behind and of being ignored.
sentences.zh: 常常感觉像是一个诞生于失望、屈辱、被抛弃感以及被忽视感的故事。

sentences.en: So in a way, we have this microcosm in Germany of what Europe looks like overall.
sentences.zh: 所以在某种程度上，我们在德国拥有一个微观世界，它反映了整个欧洲的面貌。

sentences.en: The defenders of liberal democracy are going to have to really find ways to respond to these conservative needs.
sentences.zh: 自由民主的捍卫者们将不得不真正寻找回应这些保守诉求的方法。

sentences.en: they're going to have to find a way to paint a vision of the future that speaks to people and that pays attention to people.
sentences.zh: 他们必须找到一种方式，描绘出一个能够触动人心并关注民众的未来愿景。

sentences.en: You know, and we're seeing movement.
sentences.zh: 你知道的，我们正在看到变化。

sentences.en: I mean, look at the success of the Greens in Germany and in some other countries.
sentences.zh: 我是说，看看绿党在德国和其他一些国家的成功。

sentences.en: I mean, something is definitely stirring.
sentences.zh: 我的意思是，某些事情绝对正在酝酿之中。

sentences.en: But the mainstream centrist parties, they haven't found that language of the future yet.
sentences.zh: 但是主流中间派政党，他们还没有找到那种面向未来的语言。

sentences.en: So right now, I feel like there's this large political space that's up for grabs in Europe and there's this battle going on on who's going to take that space.
sentences.zh: 所以现在，我觉得在欧洲有一个巨大的政治空间正等待着人们去争夺，一场关于谁将占据这个空间的战斗正在上演。

sentences.en: Liberal democracy is not going to win that battle if it doesn't change, if liberals don't take a very hard look at themselves.
sentences.zh: 如果自由民主不发生改变，如果自由主义者不进行深刻的反省，它是赢不了这场战斗的。

sentences.en: Because look, if the system were working for ordinary people, would we see populists rising all over the place?
sentences.zh: 因为你看，如果这个体制对普通人有效的话，我们还会看到民粹主义者到处崛起吗？

sentences.en: And if liberal democracy is not working as it is right now, can you have the European Union without it?
sentences.zh: 如果自由民主像现在这样无法运转，没有它，你还能拥有欧盟吗？

sentences.en: And what would take its place?
sentences.zh: 什么会取代它的位置呢？

sentences.en: And that's kind of the moment
sentences.zh: 这就是目前

sentences.en: Europe is in.
sentences.zh: 欧洲所处的时刻。

sentences.en: In that case, should we ask the questions?
sentences.zh: 既然如此，我们应该提出这些问题吗？

sentences.en: Okay, yeah, perfect.
sentences.zh: 好的，行，太完美了。

sentences.en: I keep thinking of the story that this Jewish restaurant owner in Chemnitz told us, the man whose restaurant was vandalized during the far-right protests that we discussed.
sentences.zh: 我一直在想起我们在开姆尼茨遇到的那位犹太餐馆老板所讲的故事，就是那个在我们在讨论的极右翼抗议活动中餐馆遭到破坏的人。

sentences.en: And I keep thinking about this thing he said.
sentences.zh: 我一直在回想他说过的那句话。

sentences.en: He said, democracy isn't permanent.
sentences.zh: 他说，民主不是永恒的。

sentences.en: Nobody ever said it was.
sentences.zh: 从来没有人说过它是。

sentences.en: He was born in the
sentences.zh: 他出生在

sentences.en: GDR in Eastern
sentences.zh: 东德的

sentences.en: Germany,
sentences.zh: 民主德国，

sentences.en: communist Germany.
sentences.zh: 也就是共产主义德国。

sentences.en: He lived in Yugoslavia.
sentences.zh: 他在南斯拉夫生活过。

sentences.en: And then he got this degree in the
sentences.zh: 然后他在

sentences.en: Soviet Union.
sentences.zh: 苏联获得了学位。

sentences.en: And now none of those countries or those systems exist anymore.
sentences.zh: 而现在，所有这些国家或体制都不复存在了。

sentences.en: They aren't on any map.
sentences.zh: 它们不在任何地图上了。

sentences.en: They failed.
sentences.zh: 它们失败了。

sentences.en: He said, how can we be so sure that democracy will survive?
sentences.zh: 他说，我们怎么能如此确信民主能够生存下去？

sentences.en: How can we be so sure that democracy won't fail too?
sentences.zh: 我们怎么能如此确信民主不会也走向失败呢？

sentences.en: Thank you.
sentences.zh: 谢谢。

sentences.en: Thank you so much.
sentences.zh: 非常感谢。

sentences.en: Thank you,
sentences.zh: 谢谢你，

sentences.en: Catherine.
sentences.zh: 凯瑟琳。

sentences.en: Thank you, guys.
sentences.zh: 谢谢你们，伙计们。

sentences.en: Okay, guys.
sentences.zh: 好了，伙计们。

sentences.en: That's a wrap.
sentences.zh: 收工了。

sentences.en: That's a wrap.
sentences.zh: 收工了。

sentences.en: Time to get a drink.
sentences.zh: 是时候去喝一杯了。

sentences.en: And some sleep.
sentences.zh: 顺便睡个觉。

sentences.en: And some sleep.
sentences.zh: 顺便睡个觉。

sentences.en: Okay, when are we doing the next show?
sentences.zh: 好吧，我们什么时候录下一期节目？

sentences.en: For decades, the Brooklyn Democratic Party operated as a tightly controlled machine.
sentences.zh: 几十年来，布鲁克林民主党一直作为一个受严密控制的机器在运作。

sentences.en: Until this summer.
sentences.zh: 直到今年夏天。

sentences.en: When elections ushered in a bunch of self-described reformers.
sentences.zh: 当时选举迎来了一群自称改革派的人士。

sentences.en: Ever since, the party has been in the grip of a bruising, chaotic, and sometimes thrilling fight.
sentences.zh: 从那以后，该党就陷入了一场残酷、混乱、有时又令人热血沸腾的争斗之中。

sentences.en: In the latest episode of Metro with me, Sarah Koenig, stories of people trying to maintain their influence and losing control along the way.
sentences.zh: 在由我萨拉·凯尼格主持的最新一期《Metro》节目中，讲述了人们试图保持影响力却在过程中失控的故事。
